description: REQ-206 claims its modification to `child-spec.js::buildChildSpec` is 'a SMALL, backward-compatible validation/signature extension' limited to the identity-anchor fields, and PROP-206d requires 'a structural diff of `child-spec.js` confirms the change is limited to required-field validation and the returned row's field list' (behavioral-spec.md:708-710). This claim is verified FALSE against the real, current source freshly re-read at `/Users/anicca/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/child-spec.js:16-34`: `buildChildSpec`'s `required` object (line 25) unconditionally requires FOUR fields this feature's REQ-201-306 chain never assigns a value or derivation rule for, and REQ-206 does not touch: `parentWallet`, `generation`, `seedUsdc`, `constitutionHash` (confirmed still mandatory-and-throwing by the file's own existing test, `child-spec.test.js:62-67`, 'buildChildSpec requires every field'). REQ-305's own EARS clause explicitly routes THIS FEATURE'S REAL spawn flow through this exact constructor ('assembled via REQ-206's identity-anchor rules ... this feature's children never carry a `childInbox`', behavioral-spec.md:846-849), meaning REQ-305's production code path -- not merely a unit-test fixture -- MUST supply concrete values for all four fields or the call throws and no ledger row is ever produced, for every single spawn attempt. None of REQ-201-306 specify: (1) `parentWallet` -- which citizen's wallet this is, when REQ-304's own edge case explicitly allows MULTIPLE different citizens to co-fund a single spawn via 'two SEPARATE single-signer transfers to the SAME child wallet' with no single 'parent' concept (behavioral-spec.md:830-833), and REQ-201 itself already generalizes the child-distinctness check away from a single parent ('distinct from ALL existing citizens," not merely the one parent that happened to initiate the attempt', behavioral-spec.md:479-480) without ever saying what value is still passed into `buildChildSpec`'s own narrower parentWallet-vs-childWallet check; (2) `generation` -- what number a colony-treasury-funded (potentially multi-citizen, non-lineage) spawn should carry; (3) `seedUsdc` -- semantically undefined in the new architecture, which instead separately tracks a 'gas seed' (REQ-204) and a 'shelter cost' (REQ-303/304), neither named or reconciled with `seedUsdc`; (4) `constitutionHash` -- embedded verbatim into the returned row's `identity` field (`"Daughter of Anicca ${constitutionHash}"`, child-spec.js:43) with zero reference anywhere in this feature to what constitution/hash a P3 spawn uses. A Phase 3 implementer cannot make REQ-305's acceptance criteria (an integration test asserting a real appended ledger row, behavioral-spec.md:904-909) pass without inventing all four values with zero spec guidance -- the opposite of REQ-206's own claim that only the identity-anchor validation changed.

additionalEvidence.note: existing test 'buildChildSpec requires every field' -- confirms all four fields (not just childInbox) still throw on omission today
REQ-206's EARS clause -- only ever discusses the childInbox/agentEvmAddress/agentId anchor fields, never parentWallet/generation/seedUsdc/constitutionHash
REQ-305's EARS explicitly routes this feature's real spawn flow through buildChildSpec
REQ-304's own edge case: multiple citizens may co-fund one spawn with no single 'parent' concept, which buildChildSpec's own real distinct-wallet check still requires (parentWallet)
PROP-206d's claim that the diff is 'limited to required-field validation and the returned row's field list' -- contradicted by the four untouched, still-mandatory fields shown above
